text:
Maya Patel: Acme reported sudden p95 latency spike ~12:01 UTC. Customer says calls usually ~200ms, now seeing ~2.6s. Sharing a trace id: 0a1b2c3d. Posting spans below for eyeballs.

Jin Park: Can you paste the span dump + request headers?

Maya Patel: span dump:```
span0 client -> edge-us-west-2 (12ms)
span1 edge-us-west-2 -> global-proxy-eu-west-1 (1200ms)  <-- unexpected cross-region hop
span2 global-proxy-eu-west-1 -> svc-eu-west-1 (30ms)
span3 svc-eu-west-1 -> ap-southeast-1-cache (900ms)
span4 svc -> edge-us-west-2 (35ms)
```
Request headers (redacted): x-redwood-region: us-west-2, x-redwood-route: default, x-api-client-id: acct-acme-01

Alex G.: That 1.2s hop from us-west edge -> eu-west proxy is the weird piece. Edge should go to regional pool or fall back to nearest compatible in same region, not jump continents.

NetworkInfra: grabbing global-egress map and recent rollouts. One sec.

Maya Patel: Repro steps I used from our prod test harness:```
curl -v \n  -H 'x-redwood-api-key: <redacted>' \n  -H 'x-redwood-region: us-west-2' \n  'https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate?model=redwood-v1'
```
Ran from a us-west agent and saw identical trace route, same unexpected eu-west hop.

Jin Park: Can you run a tcpdump on the edge host during repro and capture TLS SNI/resolved IPs? Also run `rd-trace --id 0a1b2c3d -f spans` and attach.

NetworkInfra: quick update — found rollout r-2024-11-07-gomap touched global-egress for some customer prefixes. For prefix acct-acme-01 the map incorrectly included a transit hop through eu-west-1 proxy due to an overlap rule that wasn't excluded. Looks like a config precedence bug.

Support Bot: Created incident INC-2024-421 and assigned to NetworkInfra.

Alex G.: If that's true we should rollback the rollout and add a canary that validates no cross-continent routes for region-pinned customers.

NetworkInfra: rolling back gomap entry for acct-acme-01 now (rollout rollback r-2024-11-07-gomap). Pushing change to control plane.

Maya Patel: after rollback customer reports p95 back to ~210ms. I see traces now go: edge-us-west-2 -> svc-us-west-2 -> backend (no eu hop).

Jin Park: Actions: 1) add automated test that checks routing table for region-pin customers (ticket INFRA-982), 2) add tracing alert when cross-region hop > 300ms, 3) review precedence logic in gomap builder (ticket INFRA-983).

Alex G.: Product side: can we add explicit customer config to lock egress region for high-SLO accounts? Filed PROD-416.

NetworkInfra: FYI root cause: gomap overlap rule + missing exclusion for 'customer-prefix' patterns. We'll do postmortem and include diff of the bad rollout.

Maya Patel: Customer is happy, closing their support case. Leaving this thread for the postmortem and follow-ups.

Support Bot: Incident INC-2024-421 closed (owner: NetworkInfra).
